reviews.title: Affordable and Reliable SSD Upgrade
reviews.comment: I recently purchased the TEAMGROUP AX2 512GB 2-Pack to upgrade two older PCs, and I'm quite satisfied with the results. Pros: Easy Installation: The drives were straightforward to install. I had them up and running in about 10 minutes. Amazon Performance Boost: Both PCs now boot up quickly, and applications load faster than before. Amazon Value for Money: For the price, getting two 512GB SSDs is a great deal. Cons: Not the Fastest: While there's a noticeable improvement over HDDs, these aren't the fastest SSDs available. Amazon Long-Term Reliability: I've only been using them for a few weeks, so I can't speak to their longevity yet. Overall, this SSD 2-pack is a solid choice if you're looking to breathe new life into older systems without breaking the bank.

reviews.title: Great value! Perfect for gaming!
reviews.comment: I wanted to wait a while to give this review as prolonged use would be the best way to test it. With that said, it's been a few months now and so far it has been great! My read and write speeds are fast and about what you would expect from any typical SSD. I moved all my games from my HDD to this new SSD and have noticed significantly faster loading times, and no stutter or lag whatsoever. I also bought an external case to use this in and can plug into my laptop. It fit snuggly in the case and works well for what I need it for, which is mostly as quick load storage for my Steam games. It runs silently and operating temps are maybe only a couple of degrees higher than my room temp. For the price, this is absolutely worth it! The performance/storage to value makes it an easy choice.
reviews.author: KC

reviews.title: This SSD is now a commodity for laptops.
reviews.comment: There is no way for me to test the lifetime of this SSD without a statistically significant number of samples of the product, and more than 10 years' time.  It worked when I received it, and it is still working today.  I loaded OSX onto it, and it is running an old MacBook Pro as I type.  No matter what the theorists say about SSD RAM cells not drawing current when they are not in use, if you check the stats, bigger SSDs draw more stand-by current.  I do not theoretically know why.  Perhaps it is the additional address decoders and catching registers which are not the same technology as the memory cells.  Or maybe it's just more leakage over a greater surface area.  It's not a linearly increasing load versus RAM size by any means.  A couple of TB seems to draw about double the current of this one and, hence, consume twice the power, and produce twice the heat.  I don't want my laptop power supply being bogged down like that, or the machine heating up like that.  But you do you.  If you don't have a bunch of peripherals hanging off and powered by the laptop's USB bus like I do, you probably won't burn out your laptop with 2 or 4TB.  But I'm an engineer, and I like to err on having a larger margin of safety.  512GB is way more than I can type in a lifetime, and is a plenty big enough glob of internal mass storage for me.  And I'm sure you can compare prices without my help.
